1.1: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set foorth the storie of those things, whereof we are fully persuaded,
1.2: As they have delivered them unto us, which from the beginning saw them their selves, and were ministers of ye word,
1.3: It seemed good also to me (most noble Theophilus) assoone as I had searched out perfectly all things from the beginning, to write unto thee thereof from point to point,
1.4: That thou mightest acknowledge the certaintie of those things, whereof thou hast been instructed.
1.5: In the time of Herod King of Judea, there was a certain Priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabet.
1.6: Both were just before God, and walked in all the commandements and ordinances of the Lord, without reproof.
1.7: And they had no child, because that Elisabet was barren: and both were well stricken in age.
1.8: And it came to pass, as he executed the Priestes office before God, as his course came in order,
1.9: According to the custom of the Priests office, his lot was to burn incense, when he went into the Temple of the Lord.
1.10: And the whole multitude of the people were without in prayer, while the incense was burning.
1.11: Then appeared unto him an Angel of the Lord standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
1.12: And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
1.13: But the Angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard, and thy wise Elisabet shall bear thee a sonne, and thou shalt call his name John.
1.14: And thou shalt have joy and gladnes, and many shall reioyce at his birth.
1.15: For he shalbe great in the sight of the Lord, and shall neither drink wine, nor strong drink: and he shalbe filled with the holy Ghost, even from his mothers womb.
1.16: And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to their Lord God.
1.17: For he shall goe before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisedome of the just men, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
1.18: Then Zacharias said unto ye Angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife is of a great age.
1.19: And the Angel answered, and sayde unto him, I am Gabriel that stand in the presence of God, and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these good tidings.
1.20: And behold, thou shalt be domme, and not be able to speak, until the day that these things be done, because thou beleeuedst not my words, which shalbe fulfilled in their season.
1.21: Now the people waited for Zacharias, and marueiled that he taried so long in the Temple.
1.22: And when hee came out, hee could not speak unto them: then they perceived that hee had seen a vision in the Temple: For he made signes unto them, and remained domme.
1.23: And it came to pass, when the daies of his office were fulfilled, that he departed to his own house.
1.24: And after those daies, his wife Elisabet conceived, and hid her self five moneths, saying,
1.25: Thus hath the Lord dealt with me, in the daies wherein he looked on me, to take from me my rebuke among men.
1.26: And in the sixth moneth, the Angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a citie of Galile, named Nazareth,
1.27: To a virgin affianced to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David, and the virgins name was Marie.
1.28: And the Angel went in unto her, and said, Hail thou that art freely beloved: the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
1.29: And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and thought what maner of salutation that should be.
1.30: Then the Angel said unto her, Fear not, Marie: for thou hast found fauour with God.
1.31: For loe, thou shalt conceive in thy wobe, and bear a sonne, and shalt call his name Jesus.
1.32: He shall be great, and shall be called the Sonne of the most High, and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David.
1.33: And hee shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and of his kingdom shall bee none end.
1.34: Then sayde Marie unto the Angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not man?
1.35: And the Angel answered, and said unto her, The holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall bee borne of thee, shall be called the Sonne of God.
1.36: And behold, thy cousin Elisabet, she hath also conceived a sonne in her old age: and this is her sixt moneth, which was called barren.
1.37: For with God shall nothing be vnpossible.
1.38: Then Marie said, Behold the servant of the Lord: be it unto me according to thy woorde. So the Angel departed from her.
1.39: And Marie arose in those daies, and went into ye hil countrey with hast to a citie of Juda,
1.40: And entred into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabet.
1.41: And it came to pass, as Elisabet heard the salutation of Marie, the babe sprang in her bellie, and Elisabet was filled with the holy Ghost.
1.42: And she cried with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, because the fruit of thy womb is blessed.
1.43: And whence cometh this to mee, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
1.44: For loe, assoone as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine eares, the babe sprang in my bellie for ioye,
1.45: And blessed is she that beleeued: for those things shall be perfourmed, which were told her from the Lord.
1.46: Then Marie sayde, My soul magnifieth the Lord,
1.47: And my spirit reioyceth in God my Sauiour.
1.48: For hee hath looked on the poor degree of his seruaunt: for behold, from henceforth shall all ages call me blessed,
1.49: Because hee that is mightie, hath done for me great things, and holy is his Name.
1.50: And his mercie is from generation to generation on them that fear him.
1.51: Hee hath shewed strength with his arm: hee hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
1.52: Hee hath put down the mighty from their seates, and exalted them of low degree.
1.53: Hee hath filled the hungrie with good things, and sent away the rich emptie.
1.54: Hee hath upholden Israel his seruaunt to be mindefull of his mercie
1.55: (As hee hath spoken to our fathers, to wit, to Abraham, and his seed) for ever.
1.56: And Marie abode with her about three moneths: after, she returned to her own house.
1.57: Now Elisabets time was fulfilled, that she should be delivered, and she brought foorth a sonne.
1.58: And her neighbours, and cousins heard tell how the Lord had shewed his great mercie upon her, and they reioyced with her.
1.59: And it was so that on the eight day they came to circumcise the babe, and called him Zacharias after the name of his father.
1.60: But his mother answered, and said, Not so, but he shalbe called John.
1.61: And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred, that is named with this name.
1.62: Then they made signes to his father, how he would have him called.
1.63: So hee asked for writing tables, and wrote, saying, His name is John, and they marueiled all.
1.64: And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue, and he spake and praised God.
1.65: Then fear came on all them that dwelt neere unto them, and all these woordes were noised abroad throughout all the hill countrey of Judea.
1.66: And al they that heard them, laid them up in their hearts, saying, What maner child shall this be! and the hand of the Lord was with him.
1.67: Then his father Zacharias was filled with the holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,
1.68: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, because he hath visited and redeemed his people,
1.69: And hath raised up the horn of salvation unto us, in the house of his servant David,
1.70: As he spake by ye mouth of his holy Prophets, which were since the world began, saying,
1.71: That he would send us deliverance from our enemies, and from the hands of all that hate us,
1.72: That he might shew mercie towards our fathers, and remember his holy covenant,
1.73: And the othe which he sware to our father Abraham.
1.74: Which was, that he would graunt unto us, that we being delivered out of the handes of our enemies, should serve him without fear,
1.75: All the daies of our life, in holiness and righteousness before him.
1.76: And thou, babe, shalt be called the Prophet of the most High: for thou shalt goe before the face of the Lord, to prepare his waies,
1.77: And to give knowledge of salvation unto his people, by the remission of their sinnes,
1.78: Through ye tender mercy of our God, wherby the day spring from an hie hath visited us,
1.79: To give light to them that sit in darknes, and in the shadow of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace.
1.80: And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the wilderness, til the day came that he should shew him self unto Israel.

2.1: And it came to pass in those dayes, that there came a decree from Augustus Cesar, that all the world should be taxed.
2.2: (This first taxing was made when Cyrenius was gouernour of Syria.)
2.3: Therefore went all to be taxed, every man to his own Citie.
2.4: And Joseph also went up from Galile out of a citie called Nazareth, into Judea, unto the citie of David, which is called Beth-leem (because he was of the house and linage of David,)
2.5: To bee taxed with Marie that was given him to wife, which was with child.
2.6: And so it was, that while they were there, the daies were accomplished that she should be delivered,
2.7: And she brought foorth her first begotten sonne, and wrapped him in swadling clothes, and laid him in a cratch, because there was no room for them in the ynne.
2.8: And there were in the same countrey shepheards, abiding in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.
2.9: And loe, the Angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glorie of the Lord shone about them, and they were sore afraid.
2.10: Then the Angel said unto them, Be not afraid: for behold, I bring you glad tidings of great joy, that shalbe to all the people,
2.11: That is, that unto you is borne this day in the citie of David, a Sauiour, which is Christ the Lord.
2.12: And this shalbe a sign to you, Yee shall find the babe swadled, and laid in a cratch.
2.13: And straightway there was with the Angel a multitude of heavenly souldiers, praising God, and saying,
2.14: Glory be to God in the high heavens, and peace in earth, and towards men good will.
2.15: And it came to pass whe the Angels were gone away from them into heaven, that the shepheards sayde one to another, Let us goe then unto Beth-leem, and see this thing that is come to pass which the Lord hath shewed unto us.
2.16: So they came with haste, and found both Marie and Joseph, and the babe laid in the cratch.
2.17: And when they had seen it, they published abroad the thing, that was told them of that child.
2.18: And all that heard it, wondred at ye things which were told them of the shepheards.
2.19: But Mary kept all those sayings, and pondred them in her heart.
2.20: And the shepheardes returned glorifiyng and praising God, for all that they had heard and seen as it was spoken unto them.
2.21: And when the eight daies were accomplished, that they should circumcise the child, his name was then called Jesus, which was named of the Angel, before he was conceived in the womb.
2.22: And when the daies of her purification after the Law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Hierusalem, to present him to the Lord,
2.23: (As it is written in the Law of the Lord, Every man child that first openeth ye womb, shalbe called holy to the Lord)
2.24: And to give an oblation, as it is commanded in the Law of the Lord, a pair of turtle doves, or two yong pigeons.
2.25: And behold, there was a man in Hierusalem, whose name was Simeon: this man was just, and feared God, and waited for the consolation of Israel, and the holy Ghost was upon him.
2.26: And it was declared to him from God by the holy Ghost, that he should not see death, before he had seen that Anointed of the Lord.
2.27: And he came by the motion of the spirit into the Temple, and when the parents brought in the babe Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the Law,
2.28: Then hee took him in his armes, and praised God, and sayd,
2.29: Lord, now lettest thou thy seruaunt depart in peace, according to thy woorde,
2.30: For mine eyes have seen thy salvation,
2.31: Which thou hast prepared before the face of all people,
2.32: A light to be reueiled to the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
2.33: And Joseph and his mother marueiled at those things, which were spoken touching him.
2.34: And Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother, Behold, this child is appointed for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign which shalbe spoken against,
2.35: (Yea and a sword shall pearce through thy soul) that the thoughts of many heartes may be opened.
2.36: And there was a Prophetess, one Anna the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser, which was of a great age, after she had lived with an husband seven yeeres from her virginitie:
2.37: And she was widow about four score and four yeeres, and went not out of the Temple, but served God with fastings and prayers, night and day.
2.38: She then coming at the same instant upon them, confessed likewise the Lord, and spake of him to all that looked for redemption in Hierusalem.
2.39: And when they had performed all thinges according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galile to their own citie Nazareth.
2.40: And the child grew, and waxed strong in Spirit, and was filled with wisedome, and the grace of God was with him.
2.41: Now his parents went to Hierusalem every yeere, at the feast of the Passeouer.
2.42: And when hee was twelve yeere old, and they were come up to Hierusalem, after the custom of the feast,
2.43: And had finished the dayes thereof, as they returned, the child Jesus remained in Hierusalem, and Joseph knew not, nor his mother,
2.44: But they supposing, that he had been in the company, went a dayes journey, and sought him among their kinsfolk, and acquaintance.
2.45: And when they found him not, they turned back to Hierusalem, and sought him.
2.46: And it came to pass three dayes after, that they found him in the Temple, sitting in the mids of the doctours, both hearing them, and asking them questions:
2.47: And all that heard him, were astonied at his understanding and answeres.
2.48: So when they saw him, they were amased, and his mother said unto him, Sonne, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee with very heauie hearts.
2.49: Then said he unto them, How is it that ye sought me? knew ye not that I must goe about my Fathers busines?
2.50: But they vnderstoode not the word that he spake to them.
2.51: Then hee went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subiect to them: and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
2.52: And Jesus increased in wisedome, and stature, and in fauour with God and men.

3.1: Now in the fifteenth yeere of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being gouernour of Judea, and Herod being Tetrarch of Galile, and his brother Philip Tetrarch of Iturea, and of the countrey of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the Tetrarch of Abilene,
3.2: (When Annas and Caiaphas were the hie Priestes) the word of God came unto John, the sonne of Zacharias in the wildernes.
3.3: And hee came into all the coastes about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sinnes,
3.4: As it is written in the book of the sayings of Esaias the Prophet, which saith, The voyce of him that crieth in the wildernes is, Prepare ye the way of the Lord: make his paths straight.
3.5: Every valley shalbe filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low, and crooked things shalbe made straight, and the rough wayes shalbe made smooth.
3.6: And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
3.7: Then said he to the people that were come out to be baptized of him, O generations of vipers, who hath forewarned you to flee from the wrath to come?
3.8: Bring foorth therefore fruites worthy amendment of life, and beginne not to say with your selves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
3.9: Now also is the axe layed unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not foorth good fruit, shalbe hewen down, and cast into the fire.
3.10: Then the people asked him, saying, What shall we doe then?
3.11: And he answered, and said unto them, He that hath two coates, let him part with him that hath none: and hee that hath meat, let him doe likewise.
3.12: Then came there Publicanes also to bee baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we doe?
3.13: And hee said unto them, Require no more then that which is appointed unto you.
3.14: The souldiers likewise demaunded of him, saying, And what shall we doe? And he said unto them, Doe violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely, and be content with your wages.
3.15: As the people waited, and all men mused in their heartes of John, if he were not that Christ,
3.16: John answered, and said to them all, In deed I baptize you with water, but one stronger then I, cometh, whose shoes latchet I am not worthy to unloose: hee will baptize you with the holy Ghost, and with fire.
3.17: Whose fanne is in his hand, and hee will make clean his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner, but the chaff will hee burn up with fire that never shalbe quenched.
3.18: Thus then exhorting with many other things, he preached unto the people.
3.19: But when Herod the Tetrarch was rebuked of him, for Herodias his brother Philips wife, and for all the evils which Herod had done,
3.20: He added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison.
3.21: Now it came to pass, as all the people were baptized, and that Jesus was baptized and did pray, that the heaven was opened:
3.22: And the holy Ghost came down in a bodily shape like a dove, upon him, and there was a voyce from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Sonne: in thee I am well pleased.
3.23: And Jesus himself began to bee about thirtie yeere of age, being as men supposed the sonne of Joseph, which was the sonne of Eli,
3.24: The sonne of Matthat, the sonne of Levi, the sonne of Melchi, the sonne of Janna, the sonne of Joseph,
3.25: The sonne of Mattathias, the sonne of Amos, the sonne of Naum, the sonne of Esli, the sonne of Nagge,
3.26: The sonne of Maath, the sonne of Mattathias, the sonne of Semei, the sonne of Joseph, the sonne of Juda,
3.27: The sonne of Joanna, the sonne of Rhesa, the sonne of Zorobabel, the sonne of Salathiel, the sonne of Neri,
3.28: The sonne of Melchi, the sonne of Addi, the sonne of Cosam, the sonne of Elmodam, the sonne of Er,
3.29: The sonne of Jose, the sonne of Eliezer, the sonne of Jorim, the sonne of Matthat, the son of Levi,
3.30: The sonne of Simeon, the sonne of Juda, the sonne of Joseph, the sonne of Jonan, the sonne of Eliacim,
3.31: The sonne of Melea, the sonne of Mainan, the sonne of Mattatha, the sonne of Nathan, the sonne of David,
3.32: The sonne of Jesse, the sonne of Obed, the sonne of Booz, the sonne of Salmon, the sonne of Naasson,
3.33: The sonne of Aminadab, the sonne of Aram, the sonne of Esrom, the sonne of Phares, the sonne of Juda,
3.34: The sonne of Jacob, the sonne of Isaac, the sonne of Abraham, the sonne of Thara, the sonne of Nachor,
3.35: The sonne of Saruch, the sonne of Ragau, the sonne of Phalec, the sonne of Eber, the sonne of Sala,
3.36: The sonne of Cainan, the sonne of Arphaxad, the sonne of Sem, the sonne of Noe, the sonne of Lamech,
3.37: The sonne of Mathusala, the sonne of Enoch, the sonne of Jared, the sonne of Maleleel, the sonne of Cainan,
3.38: The sonne of Enos, the sonne of Seth, the sonne of Adam, the sonne of God.

4.1: And Jesus full of the holy Ghost returned from Jordan, and was led by that Spirit into the wildernes,
4.2: And was there fourtie dayes tempted of the devil, and in those dayes he did eat nothing: but when they were ended, he afterward was hungry.
4.3: Then the devil said unto him, If thou be the Sonne of God, commaund this stone that it be made bread.
4.4: But Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread only, but by every word of God.
4.5: Then the devil took him up into an high mountain, and shewed him all the kingdomes of the world, in the twinkeling of an eye.
4.6: And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of those kingdomes: for that is delivered to mee: and to whomsoever I will, I give it.
4.7: If thou therefore wilt worship mee, they shalbe all thine.
4.8: But Jesus answered him, and said, Hence from mee, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him alone thou shalt serve.
4.9: Then hee brought him to Hierusalem, and set him on a pinacle of the Temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Sonne of God, cast thy self down from hence,
4.10: For it is written, That hee will give his Angels charge over thee to keep thee:
4.11: And with their handes they shall lift thee up, least at any time thou shouldest dash thy foot against a stone.
4.12: And Jesus answered, and said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
4.13: And when the devil had ended all the tentation, he departed from him for a litle season.
4.14: And Jesus returned by the power of the spirit into Galile: and there went a fame of him throughout all the region round about.
4.15: For he taught in their Synagogues, and was honoured of all men.
4.16: And hee came to Nazareth where hee had been brought up, and (as his custom was) went into the Synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
4.17: And there was delivered unto him the book of the Prophet Esaias: and when hee had opened the book, hee found the place, where it was written,
4.18: The Spirit of the Lord is upon mee, because he hath anoynted me, that I should preach the Gospel to the poor: he hath sent mee, that I should heal the broken hearted, that I should preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, that I should set at libertie them that are bruised:
4.19: And that I should preach the acceptable yeere of the Lord.
4.20: And hee closed the book, and gave it again to the minister, and sat down: and the eyes of all that were in the Synagogue were fastened on him.
4.21: Then he began to say unto them, This day is the Scripture fulfilled in your eares.
4.22: And all bare him witnes, and wondered at the gracious wordes, which proceeded out of his mouth, and said, Is not this Iosephs sonne?
4.23: Then he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto mee this proverb, Physician, heal thy self: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, doe it here likewise in thine own countrey.
4.24: And he said, Verely I say unto you, No Prophet is accepted in his own countrey.
4.25: But I tell you of a trueth, many widowes were in Israel in the dayes of Elias, when heaven was shut three yeres and six moneths, when great famine was throughout all the land:
4.26: But unto none of them was Elias sent, save into Sarepta, a citie of Sidon, unto a certain widow.
4.27: Also many lepers were in Israel, in the time of Eliseus the Prophet: yet none of them was made clean, saving Naaman the Syrian.
4.28: Then all that were in the Synagogue, when they heard it, were filled with wrath,
4.29: And rose up, and thrust him out of the citie, and led him unto the edge of the hil, whereon their citie was built, to cast him down headlong.
4.30: But he passed through the middes of them, and went his way,
4.31: And came down into Capernaum a citie of Galile, and there taught them on the Sabbath dayes.
4.32: And they were astonied at his doctrine: for his word was with authoritie.
4.33: And in the Synagogue there was a man which had a spirit of an vncleane devil, which cryed with a loud voyce,
4.34: Saying, Oh, what have we to doe with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know who thou art, even the holy one of God.
4.35: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. Then the devil throwing him in the middes of them, came out of him, and hurt him nothing at all.
4.36: So fear came on them all, and they spake among themselves, saying, What thing is this: for with authoritie and power he commaundeth the fowl spirits, and they come out?
4.37: And ye fame of him spred abroad throughout all the places of the countrey round about.
4.38: And he rose up, and came out of the Synagogue, and entred into Simons house. And Simons wives mother was taken with a great fever, and they required him for her.
4.39: Then he stood over her, and rebuked the fever, and it left her, and immediatly she arose, and ministred unto them.
4.40: Now at the sunne setting, all they that had sick folkes of divers diseases, brought them unto him, and he layd his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
4.41: And devils also came out of many, crying, and saying, Thou art that Christ that Sonne of God: but he rebuked them, and suffered them not to say that they knew him to be that Christ.
4.42: And when it was day, he departed, and went foorth into a desart place, and the people sought him, and came to him, and kept him that he should not depart from them.
4.43: But he sayd unto them, Surely I must also preach the kingdom of God to other cities: for therefore am I sent.
4.44: And hee preached in the Synagogues of Galile.

5.1: Then it came to pass, as the people preassed upon him to hear the word of God, that he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,
5.2: And saw two shippes stand by the lakes side, but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nettes.
5.3: And he entred into one of the ships, which was Simons, and required him that he would thrust off a litle from the land: and he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.
5.4: Now when he had left speaking, he sayd unto Simon, Lanch out into the deep, and let down your nettes to make a draught.
5.5: Then Simon answered, and sayd unto him, Master, we have travailed sore all night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.
5.6: And when they had so done, they enclosed a great multitude of fishes, so that their net brake.
5.7: And they beckened to their parteners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them, who came then, and filled both the ships, that they did sink.
5.8: Now when Simon Peter saw it, he fel down at Jesus knees, saying, Lord, go from me: for I am a sinful man.
5.9: For he was utterly astonied, and all that were with him, for the draught of fishes which they took.
5.10: And so was also James and John the sonnes of Zebedeus, which were companions with Simon. Then Jesus sayde unto Simon, Fear not: from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
5.11: And when they had brought the ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
5.12: Now it came to pass, as he was in a certain citie, behold, there was a man full of leprosie, and when he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
5.13: So he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will, be thou clean. And immediately the leprosie departed from him.
5.14: And he commanded him that hee should tell it no man: but Go, sayth he, and shew thy self to the Priest, and offer for thy clensing, as Moses hath commanded, for a witnes unto them.
5.15: But so much more went there a fame abroad of him, and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed of him of their infirmities.
5.16: But he kept himself apart in the wildernes, and prayed.
5.17: And it came to pass, on a certain day, as he was teaching, that the Pharises and doctours of the Law sat by, which were come out of every town of Galile, and Judea, and Hierusalem, and the power of the Lord was in him to heal them.
5.18: Then behold, men brought a man lying in a bed, which was taken with a palsie, and they sought meanes to bring him in, and to lay him before him.
5.19: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in, because of the preasse, they went up on the house, and let him down through the tyling, bed and all, in the middes before Jesus.
5.20: And when he saw their faith, he sayd unto him, Man, thy sinnes are forgiven thee.
5.21: Then the Scribes and the Pharises began to reason, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? who can forgive sinnes, but God onely?
5.22: But when Jesus perceived their reasoning, he answered, and sayd unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?
5.23: Whether is easier to say, Thy sinnes are forgiven thee, or to say, Rise and walk?
5.24: But that ye may know that that Sonne of man hath authoritie to forgive sinnes in earth, (he sayd unto the sick of the palsie) I say to thee, Arise: take up thy bed, and goe to thine house.
5.25: And immediatly he rose up before them, and took up his bed whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, praysing God.
5.26: And they were all amased, and praysed God, and were filled with fear, saying, Doutlesse we have seen strange things to day.
5.27: And after that, he went foorth and saw a Publican named Levi, sitting at the receite of custom, and sayd unto him, Follow me.
5.28: And he left all, rose up, and folowed him.
5.29: Then Levi made him a great feast in his own house, where there was a great company of Publicanes, and of other that sat at table with them.
5.30: But they that were Scribes and Pharises among them, murmured against his disciples, saying, Why eat ye and drink ye with Publicanes and sinners?
5.31: Then Jesus answered, and sayd unto them, They that are whole, need not the Physician, but they that are sick.
5.32: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
5.33: Then they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and pray, and the disciples of the Pharises also, but thine eat and drink?
5.34: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the wedding chamber to fast, as long as the bridegrome is with them?
5.35: But the dayes will come, even when the bridegrome shalbe taken away from them: then shall they fast in those dayes.
5.36: Again he spake also unto them a parable, No man putteth a piece of a new garment into an old vesture: for then the new renteth it, and the piece taken out of the new, agreeth not with the old.
5.37: Also no man powreth new wine into old vessels: for then ye new wine wil break the vessels, and it will runne out, and the vessels will perish:
5.38: But new wine must be powred into new vessels: so both are preserved.
5.39: Also no man that drinketh old wine, straightway desireth new: for he sayth, The old is more profitable.

6.1: And it came to pass on a second solemn Sabbath, that hee went through the corn fieldes, and his disciples plucked the eares of corn, and did eat, and rub them in their hands.
6.2: And certain of the Pharises sayde unto them, Why doe ye that which is not lawful to doe on the Sabbath dayes?
6.3: Then Jesus answered them, and said, Have ye not read this, that David did when he himself was an hungred, and they which were with him,
6.4: How he went into the house of God, and took, and ate the shewbread, and gave also to them which were with him, which was not lawful to eat, but for the Priests onely?
6.5: And he sayd unto them, The Sonne of man is Lord also of the Sabbath day.
6.6: It came to pass also on another Sabbath, that hee entred into the Synagogue, and taught, and there was a man, whose right hand was dryed up.
6.7: And the Scribes and Pharises watched him, whether he would heal on the Sabbath day, that they might find an accusation against him.
6.8: But he knew their thoughts, and sayd to the man which had the withered hand, Arise, and stand up in the middes. And hee arose, and stood up.
6.9: Then sayd Jesus unto them, I will ask you a question, Whether is it lawful on the Sabbath dayes to doe good, or to doe evil? to save life, or to destroy?
6.10: And he beheld them all in compass, and sayd unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he did so, and his hand was restored again, as whole as the other.
6.11: Then they were filled full of madnes, and communed one with another, what they might doe to Jesus.
6.12: And it came to pass in those dayes, that he went into a mountain to pray, and spent the night in prayer to God.
6.13: And when it was day, he called his disciples, and of them he chose twelve which also he called Apostles.
6.14: (Simon whom he named also Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philippe and Bartlemewe:
6.15: Matthew and Thomas: James the sonne of Alpheus, and Simon called Zelous,
6.16: Judas James brother, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitour.)
6.17: Then he came down with them, and stood in a plain place, with the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judea, and Hierusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyrus and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases:
6.18: And they that were vexed with fowl spirits, and they were healed.
6.19: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went vertue out of him, and healed them all.
6.20: And hee lifted up his eyes upon his disciples, and sayd, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
6.21: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shalbe satisfied: blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
6.22: Blessed are ye when men hate you, and when they separate you, and revile you, and put out your name as evil, for the Sonne of mans sake.
6.23: Reioyce ye in that day, and be glad: for behold, your reward is great in heaven: for after this maner their fathers did to the Prophets.
6.24: But wo be to you that are rich: for ye have received your consolation.
6.25: Wo be to you that are full: for ye shall hunger. Wo be to you that now laugh: for ye shall wayle and weep.
6.26: Wo be to you when all men speak well of you: for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
6.27: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies: doe well to them which hate you.
6.28: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which hurt you.
6.29: And unto him that smiteth thee on ye one cheek, offer also the other: and him that taketh away thy cloke, forbid not to take thy coat also.
6.30: Give to every man that asketh of thee: and of him that taketh away the things that be thine, ask them not again.
6.31: And as ye would that men should doe to you, so doe ye to them likewise.
6.32: For if yee love them which love you, what thank shall ye have? for even the sinners love those that love them.
6.33: And if ye do good for them which do good for you, what thank shall ye have? for even the sinners doe the same.
6.34: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank shall yee have? for even the sinners lend to sinners, to receive the like.
6.35: Wherefore love ye your enemies, and doe good, and lend, looking for nothing again, and your reward shalbe great, and ye shalbe the children of the most High: for he is kind unto the vnkinde, and to the evil.
6.36: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
6.37: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not bee condemned: forgive, and ye shalbe forgiven.
6.38: Give, and it shalbe given unto you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over shall men give into your bosom: for with what measure ye mete, with the same shall men mete to you again.
6.39: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?
6.40: The disciple is not above his master: but whosoever will be a perfect disciple, shall bee as his master.
6.41: And why seest thou a mote in thy brothers eye, and considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
6.42: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou seest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Hypocrite, cast out the beam out of thine own eye first, and then shalt thou see, perfectly to pull out the mote that is in thy brothers eye.
6.43: For it is not a good tree that bringeth foorth evil fruit: neither an evil tree, that bringeth foorth good fruit.
6.44: For every tree is knowen by his own fruit: for neither of thornes gather men figges, nor of bushes gather they grapes.
6.45: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth foorth good, and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth foorth evil: for of the aboundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.
6.46: But why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things that I speak?
6.47: Whosoever cometh to mee, and heareth my wordes, and doeth the same, I will shew you to whom he is like:
6.48: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and layde the fundation on a rock: and when the waters arose, the flood beat upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was grounded upon a rock.
6.49: But hee that heareth and doeth not, is like a man that built an house upon the earth without foundation, against which the flood did beat, and it fell by and by: and the fall of that house was great.

7.1: When hee had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entred into Capernaum.
7.2: And a certain Ceturions servant was sick and readie to die, which was dear unto him.
7.3: And when he heard of Jesus, hee sent unto him the Elders of the Iewes, beseeching him that he would come, and heal his servant.
7.4: So they came to Jesus, and besought him instantly, saying that hee was worthy that hee should doe this for him:
7.5: For he loveth, said they, our nation, and he hath built us a Synagogue.
7.6: Then Jesus went with them: but when he was now not far from the house, the Centurion sent friendes to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thy self: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
7.7: Wherefore I thought not my self worthy to come unto thee: but say the word, and my servant shalbe whole:
7.8: For I likewise am a man set under authoritie, and have under mee souldiers, and I say unto one, Goe, and he goeth: and to another, Come, and hee cometh: and to my servant, Doe this, and he doeth it.
7.9: When Jesus heard these things, he marueiled at him, and turned him, and said to the people, that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no not in Israel.
7.10: And when they that were sent, turned back to the house, they found the servant that was sick, whole.
7.11: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a citie called Nain, and many of his disciples went with him, and a great multitude.
7.12: Now when hee came neere to the gate of the citie, behold, there was a dead man caried out, who was the onely begotten sonne of his mother, which was a widow, and much people of the citie was with her.
7.13: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
7.14: And he went and touched the coffin (and they that bare him, stood still) and he said, Yong man, I say unto thee, Arise.
7.15: And he that was dead, sat up, and began to speak, and he delivered him to his mother.
7.16: Then there came a fear on them all, and they glorified God, saying, A great Prophet is risen among us, and God hath visited his people.
7.17: And this rumour of him went foorth throughout all Judea, and throughout all the region round about.
7.18: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.
7.19: So John called unto him two certain men of his disciples, and sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou hee that should come, or shall we wait for another?
7.20: And when the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou hee that should come, or shall we wait for another?
7.21: And at that time, he cured many of their sickenesses, and plagues, and of evil spirites, and unto many blind men he gave sight freely.
7.22: And Jesus answered, and said unto them, Goe your wayes and shew John, what things ye have seen and heard: that the blind see, the halt goe, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor receive the Gospel.
7.23: And blessed is hee, that shall not be offended in me.
7.24: And when the messengers of John were departed, hee began to speak unto the people, of John, What went ye out into the wildernes to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
7.25: But what went ye out to see? A man clothed in soft rayment? behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in Kings courtes.
7.26: But what went ye foorth to see? A Prophet? yea, I say to you, and greater then a Prophet.
7.27: This is he of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
7.28: For I say unto you, there is no greater Prophet then John, among them that are begotten of women: nevertheless, hee that is the least in the kingdom of God, is greater then he.
7.29: Then all the people that heard, and the Publicanes justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
7.30: But the Pharises and the expounders of the Law despised the counsel of God against themselves, and were not baptized of him.
7.31: And the Lord said, Whereunto shall I liken the men of this generation? and what thing are they like unto?
7.32: They are like unto litle children sitting in the market place, and crying one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not daunced: we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
7.33: For John Baptist came, neither eating bread, nor drinking wine: and ye say, He hath the devil.
7.34: The Sonne of man is come, and eateth and drinketh: and ye say, Behold, a man which is a glutton, and a drinker of wine, a friend of Publicanes and sinners:
7.35: But wisdom is justified of all her children.
7.36: And one of the Pharises desired him that hee would eat with him: and hee went into the Pharises house, and sat down at table.
7.37: And behold, a woman in the citie, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at table in the Pharises house, she brought a box of oyntment.
7.38: And she stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with teares, and did wipe them with the heares of her head, and kissed his feet, and anoynted them with the oyntment.
7.39: Now when the Pharise which bade him, saw it, he spake within himself, saying, If this man were a Prophet, hee would surely have knowen who, and what maner of woman this is which toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
7.40: And Jesus answered, and said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he said, Master, say on.
7.41: There was a certain lender which had two detters: the one ought five hundreth pence, and the other fiftie:
7.42: When they had nothing to pay, he forgave them both: Which of them therefore, tell mee, will love him most?
7.43: Simon answered, and said, I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast truely judged.
7.44: Then he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entred into thine house, and thou gavest mee no water to my feet: but she hath washed my feet with teares, and wiped them with the heares of her head.
7.45: Thou gavest me no kiss: but she, since the time I came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.
7.46: Mine head with oyle thou didest not anoint: but she hath anoynted my feet with oyntment.
7.47: Wherefore I say unto thee, many sinnes are forgiven her: for she loved much. To whom a litle is forgiven, he doeth love a litle.
7.48: And he said unto her, Thy sinnes are forgiven thee.
7.49: And they that sat at table with him, began to say within themselves, Who is this that even forgiveth sinnes?
7.50: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee: goe in peace.

8.1: And it came to pass afterward, that hee himself went through every citie and town, preaching and publishing the kingdom of God, and the twelve were with him,
8.2: And certain women, which were healed of evil spirites, and infirmities, as Mary which was called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,
8.3: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herods steward, and Susanna, and many other which ministred unto him of their substance.
8.4: Now when much people were gathered together, and were come unto him out of all cities, he spake by a parable.
8.5: A sower went out to sow his seed, and as he sowed, some fell by the wayes side, and it was troden under feet, and the foules of heaven deuoured it up.
8.6: And some fell on the stones, and when it was sprong up, it withered away, because it lacked moystnesse.
8.7: And some fell among thornes, and the thornes sprang up with it, and choked it.
8.8: And some fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit, an hundreth fold. And as hee sayd these things, he cryed, He that hath eares to hear, let him hear.
8.9: Then his disciples asked him, demaunding what parable that was.
8.10: And he sayd, Unto you it is given to know the secrets of ye kingdom of God, but to other in parables, that when they see, they should not see, and when they hear, they should not understand.
8.11: The parable is this, The seed is the word of God.
8.12: And they that are beside the way, are they that hear: afterward cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, least they should beleeue, and be saved.
8.13: But they that are on the stones, are they which when they have heard, receive ye word with joy: but they have no rootes: which for a while beleeue, but in the time of tentation goe away.
8.14: And that which fell among thornes, are they which have heard, and after their departure are choked with cares and with riches, and voluptuous living, and bring forth no fruit.
8.15: But that which fell in good ground, are they which with an honest and good heart hear the word, and keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
8.16: No man when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it under a vessell, neither putteth it under the bed, but setteth it on a candlestick, that they that enter in, may see the light.
8.17: For nothing is secret, that shall not be evident: neither any thing hid, that shall not be knowen, and come to light.
8.18: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given: and whosoever hath not, from him shalbe taken even that which it seemeth that he hath.
8.19: Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come neere to him for the preasse.
8.20: And it was told him by certain which said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, and would see thee.
8.21: But he answered, and sayd unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and doe it.
8.22: And it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples, and he sayd unto them, Let us goe over unto the other side of the lake. And they lanched forth.
8.23: And as they sayled, he fell a sleep, and there came down a storm of wind on the lake, and they were filled with water, and were in ieopardie.
8.24: Then they went to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, Master, we perish. And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and the waves of water: and they ceased, and it was calm.
8.25: Then he sayde unto them, Where is your fayth? and they feared, and wondered among them selves, saying, Who is this that commandeth both the windes and water, and they obey him!
8.26: So they sailed unto the region of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galile.
8.27: And as he went out to land, there met him a certain man out of the citie, which had devils long time, and he ware no garment, neither abode in house, but in the graves.
8.28: And when he saw Jesus, he cryed out and fell down before him, and with a loud voyce sayd, What have I to doe with thee, Jesus the Sonne of God the most High? I beseech thee torment me not.
8.29: For he commanded ye fowl spirit to come out of the man: (for oft times he had caught him: therefore he was bound with chaines, and kept in fetters: but he brake the bands, and was caried of the devil into wildernesses.)
8.30: Then Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? and he sayd, Legion, because many devils were entred into him.
8.31: And they besought him, that he would not commaund them to goe out into the deep.
8.32: And there was there by, an heard of many swine, feeding on an hill: and the devils besought him, that he would suffer them to enter into them. So he suffered them.
8.33: Then went the devils out of the man, and entred into the swine: and the heard was caried with violence from a steep down place into the lake, and was choked.
8.34: When the heardmen saw what was done, they fled: and when they were departed, they told it in the citie and in the countrey.
8.35: Then they came out to see what was done, and came to Jesus, and found the man, out of whom the devils were departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afrayd.
8.36: They also which saw it, told them by what meanes he that was possessed with the devil, was healed.
8.37: Then the whole multitude of the countrey about the Gadarenes, besought him that he would depart from them: for they were taken with a great fear: and he went into the ship, and returned.
8.38: Then the man, out of whom the devils were departed, besought him that hee might be with him: but Jesus sent him away, saying,
8.39: Return into thine own house, and shew what great things God hath done to thee. So hee went his way, and preached throughout all the citie, what great things Jesus had done unto him.
8.40: And it came to pass, when Jesus was come again, that the people received him: for they all waited for him.
8.41: And behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was the ruler of the Synagogue, who fell down at Jesus feet, and besought him that he would come into his house.
8.42: For he had but a daughter onely, about twelve yeeres of age, and she lay a dying (and as he went, the people thronged him.
8.43: And a woman having an yssue of blood, twelve yeeres long, which had spent all her substance upon physicians, and could not be healed of any:
8.44: When she came behind him, she touched the hemme of his garment, and immediatly her yssue of blood stanched.
8.45: Then Jesus sayd, Who is it that hath touched me? When every man denied, Peter sayd and they that were with him, Master, the multitude thrust thee, and tread on thee, and sayest thou, Who hath touched me?
8.46: And Jesus sayde, Some one hath touched me: for I perceive that vertue is gone out of me.
8.47: When the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and fell down before him, and told him before all the people, for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed immediatly.
8.48: And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath saved thee: go in peace.)
8.49: While he yet spake, there came one from the ruler of the Synagogues house, which sayde to him, Thy daughter is dead: disease not the Master.
8.50: When Jesus heard it, he answered him, saying, Fear not: beleeue onely, and she shall be saved.
8.51: And when he went into the house, he suffered no man to goe in with him, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and mother of the maid.
8.52: And all wept, and sorowed for her: but he sayd, Weep not: for she is not dead, but sleepeth.
8.53: And they laught him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.
8.54: So he thrust them all out, and took her by the hand, and cryed, saying, Maid, arise.
8.55: And her spirit came again, and she rose straightway: and he comanded to give her meat.
8.56: Then her parents were astonied: but hee commanded them that they should tell no man what was done.

9.1: Then called hee his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authoritie over all devils, and to heal diseases.
9.2: And hee sent them foorth to preach the kingdom of God, and to cure the sick.
9.3: And he sayd to them, Take nothing to your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, nor silver, neither have two coates apiece.
9.4: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.
9.5: And how many so ever will not receive you, when ye goe out of that citie, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimonie against them.
9.6: And they went out, and went through every town preaching the Gospel, and healing every where.
9.7: Now Herod the Tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he douted, because that it was sayd of some, that John was risen again from the dead:
9.8: And of some, that Elias had appeared: and of some, that one of the old Prophets was risen again.
9.9: Then Herod sayd, John have I beheaded: who then is this of whom I hear such things? and he desired to see him.
9.10: And when the Apostles returned, they told him what great things they had done. Then he took them to him, and went aside into a solitarie place, neere to the citie called Bethsaida.
9.11: But when the people knew it, they followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need to be healed.
9.12: And when the day began to wear away, the twelve came, and sayd unto him, Send the people away, that they may goe into the townes and villages round about, and lodge, and get meat: for we are here in a desart place.
9.13: But he sayd unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they sayd, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes, except we should go and buy meat for all this people.
9.14: For they were about five thousand men. Then he sayde to his disciples, Cause them to sit down by fifties in a company.
9.15: And they did so, and caused all to sit down.
9.16: Then he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looked up to heaven, and blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples, to set before the people.
9.17: So they did all eat, and were satisfied: and there was taken up of that remained to them, twelve baskets full of broken meat.
9.18: And it came to pass, as hee was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
9.19: They answered, and sayd, John Baptist: and others say, Elias: and some say, that one of the old Prophets is risen again.
9.20: And he sayd unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answered, and sayd, That Christ of God.
9.21: And he warned and commanded them, that they should tell that to no man,
9.22: Saying, The Sonne of man must suffer many things and be reproved of the Elders, and of the hie Priests and Scribes, and be slain, and the third day rise again.
9.23: And he sayd to them all, If any man will come after me, let him denie himself, and take up his cross dayly, and follow me.
9.24: For whosoever will save his life, shall lose it: and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
9.25: For what auantageth it a man, if he win the whole world, and destroy himself, or lose himself?
9.26: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me, and of my wordes, of him shall the Sonne of man be ashamed, when hee shall come in his glorie, and in the glorie of the Father, and of the holy Angels.
9.27: And I tell you of a suretie, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God.
9.28: And it came to pass about an eyght dayes after those wordes, that he took Peter and John, and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
9.29: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was changed, and his garment was white and glistered.
9.30: And behold, two men talked with him, which were Moses and Elias:
9.31: Which appeared in glory, and told of his departing, which he should accomplish at Hierusalem.
9.32: But Peter and they that were with him, were heauie with sleep, and when they awoke, they saw his glorie, and the two men standing with him.
9.33: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: let us therefore make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias, and wist not what he said.
9.34: Whiles he thus spake, there came a cloud and overshadowed them, and they feared when they were entring into the cloud.
9.35: And there came a voyce out of the cloud, saying, This is that my beloved Sonne, hear him.
9.36: And when the voyce was past, Jesus was found alone: and they kept it close, and told no man in those dayes any of those things which they had seen.
9.37: And it came to pass on the next day, as they came down from the mountain, much people met him.
9.38: And behold, a man of the companie cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, behold my sonne: for he is all that I have.
9.39: And loe, a spirit taketh him, and suddenly he crieth, and he teareth him, that he fometh, and hardly departeth from him, when he hath bruised him.
9.40: Now I have besought thy disciples to cast him out, but they could not.
9.41: Then Jesus answered, and said, O generation faithless, and crooked, how long now shall I be with you, and suffer you? bring thy sonne hither.
9.42: And whiles he was yet coming, the devil rent him, and tare him: and Jesus rebuked the vncleane spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him to his father.
9.43: And they were all amased at the mightie power of God: and while they all wondered at al things, which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,
9.44: Mark these wordes diligently: for it shall come to pass, that the Sonne of man shalbe delivered into the handes of men.
9.45: But they understood not that word: for it was hid from them, so that they could not perceive it: and they feared to ask him of that word.
9.46: Then there arose a disputation among them, which of them should be the greatest.
9.47: When Jesus saw the thoughtes of their heartes, he took a litle child, and set him by him,
9.48: And said unto them, Whosoever receiveth this litle child in my Name, receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me, receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, he shall be great.
9.49: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy Name, and we forbad him, because he followeth thee not with us.
9.50: Then Jesus said unto him, Forbid ye him not: for he that is not against us, is with us.
9.51: And it came to pass, when the dayes were accomplished, that he should be received up, he setled himself fully to goe to Hierusalem,
9.52: And sent messengers before him: and they went and entred into a town of the Samaritans, to prepare him lodging.
9.53: But they would not receive him, because his behauiour was, as though he would go to Hierusalem.
9.54: And when his disciples, James and John saw it, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we commaund, that fire come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
9.55: But Jesus turned about, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not of what spirit ye are.
9.56: For the Sonne of man is not come to destroy mens lives, but to save them. Then they went to another town.
9.57: And it came to pass that as they went in the way, a certain man said unto him, I will follow thee, Lord, whithersoever thou goest.
9.58: And Jesus said unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birdes of the heaven nestes, but the Sonne of man hath not whereon to lay his head.
9.59: But he said unto another, Follow me. And the same said, Lord, suffer me first to goe and burie my father.
9.60: And Jesus said unto him, Let the dead burie their dead: but go thou, and preach the kingdom of God.
9.61: Then another said, I will follow thee, Lord: but let me first go bid them farewell, which are at mine house.
9.62: And Jesus said unto him, No man that putteth his hand to the plough, and looketh back, is apt to the kingdom of God.

10.1: After these thinges, the Lord appointed other seuentie also, and sent them, two and two before him into every citie and place, whither he himself should come.
10.2: And he said unto them, The harvest is great, but the labourers are few: pray therefore the Lord of the harvest to send foorth labourers into his harvest.
10.3: Goe your wayes: behold, I send you foorth as lambes among wolves.
10.4: Bear no bagge, neither scrippe, nor shoes, and salute no man by the way.
10.5: And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
10.6: And if the sonne of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon him: if not, it shall turn to you again.
10.7: And in that house tary still, eating and drinking such things as by them shall be set before you: for the labourer is worthy of his wages. Goe not from house to house.
10.8: But into whatsoever citie ye shall enter, if they receive you, eat such things as are set before you,
10.9: And heal the sick that are there, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come neere unto you.
10.10: But into whatsoever citie ye shall enter, if they will not receive you, goe your wayes out into the streetes of the same, and say,
10.11: Even the very dust, which cleaveth on us of your citie, we wipe off against you: notwithstanding know this, that the kingdom of God was come neere unto you.
10.12: For I say to you, that it shall be easier in that day for them of Sodom, then for that citie.
10.13: Woe be to thee, Chorazin: woe be to thee, Beth-saida: for if the miracles had been done in Tyrus and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while agone repented, sitting in sackecloth and ashes.
10.14: Therefore it shall be easier for Tyrus, and Sidon, at the iudgement, then for you.
10.15: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.
10.16: He that heareth you, heareth me: and he that despiseth you, despiseth me: and he that despiseth me, despiseth him that sent me.
10.17: And the seuentie turned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subdued to us through thy Name.
10.18: And he said unto them, I saw Satan, like lightening, fall down from heaven.
10.19: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on Serpents, and Scorpions, and over all the power of the enemie, and nothing shall hurt you.
10.20: Nevertheless, in this reioyce not, that the spirits are subdued unto you: but rather reioyce, because your names are written in heaven.
10.21: That same hour reioyced Jesus in the spirit, and said, I confess unto thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and understanding, and hast reueiled them to babes: even so, Father, because it so pleased thee.
10.22: All things are given me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Sonne is, but the Father: neither who the Father is, save the Sonne, and he to whom the Sonne will reueile him.
10.23: And he turned to his disciples, and said secretly, Blessed are the eyes, which see that ye see.
10.24: For I tell you that many Prophets and Kings have desired to see those things, which ye see, and have not seen them: and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.
10.25: Then behold, a certain Lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I doe, to inherit eternal life?
10.26: And he said unto him, What is written in the Law? how readest thou?
10.27: And he answered, and said, Thou shalt love thy Lord God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy thought, and thy neighbour as thy self.
10.28: Then he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this doe, and thou shalt live.
10.29: But he willing to iustifie himself, said unto Jesus, Who is then my neighbour?
10.30: And Jesus answered, and said, A certain man went down from Hierusalem to Jericho, and fell among theeues, and they robbed him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
10.31: Now so it fell out, that there came down a certain Priest that same way, and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
10.32: And likewise also a Levite, when he was come neere to the place, went and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
10.33: Then a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came neere unto him, and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
10.34: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, and powred in oyle and wine, and put him on his own beast, and brought him to an Inn, and made provision for him.
10.35: And on the morowe when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him, and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will recompense thee.
10.36: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the theeues?
10.37: And he said, He that shewed mercie on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Goe, and do thou likewise.
10.38: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entred into a certain town, and a certain woman named Martha, received him into her house.
10.39: And she had a sister called Marie, which also sat at Jesus feet, and heard his preaching.
10.40: But Martha was combred about much serving, and came to him, and said, Master, doest thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore, that she help me.
10.41: And Jesus answered, and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou carest, and art troubled about many things:
10.42: But one thing is needefull, Marie hath chosen the good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

11.1: And so it was, that as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.
11.2: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Our Father, which art in heaven, halowed be thy Name: Thy kingdom come: Let thy will be done, even in earth, as it is in heaven:
11.3: Our dayly bread give us for the day:
11.4: And forgive us our sinnes: for even we forgive every man that is indetted to us: And lead us not into temptation: but deliver us from evil.
11.5: Moreover he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall goe to him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend mee three loaves?
11.6: For a friend of mine is come out of the way to me, and I have nothing to set before him:
11.7: And hee within should answer, and say, Trouble mee not: the door is now shut, and my children are with mee in bed: I can not rise and give them to thee.
11.8: I say unto you, Though he would not arise and give him, because he is his friend, yet doubtless because of his importunitie, hee would rise, and give him as many as he needed.
11.9: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you: seek, and yee shall find: knock, and it shalbe opened unto you.
11.10: For every one that asketh, receiveth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shalbe opened.
11.11: If a sonne shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if hee ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?
11.12: Or if hee ask an egg, will hee give him a scorpion?
11.13: If yee then which are evil, can give good giftes unto your children, how much more shall your heavenly Father give the holy Ghost to them, that desire him?
11.14: Then hee cast out a devil which was domme: and when the devil was gone out, the domme spake, and the people wondered.
11.15: But some of them said, He casteth out devils through Beelzebub the chief of ye devils.
11.16: And others tempted him, seeking of him a sign from heaven.
11.17: But he knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom deuided against it self, shall be desolate, and an house deuided against an house, falleth.
11.18: So if Satan also bee deuided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand, because yee say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub?
11.19: If I through Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom doe your children cast them out? Therefore shall they be your judges.
11.20: But if I by ye finger of God cast out devils, doutles the kingdom of God is come unto you.
11.21: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, the thinges that hee possesseth, are in peace.
11.22: But when a stronger then hee, cometh upon him, and overcometh him: hee taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and deuideth his spoiles.
11.23: He that is not with me, is against me: and he that gathereth not with me, scattereth.
11.24: When the vncleane spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through drie places, seeking rest: and when he findeth none he saieth, I wil return unto mine house whence I came out.
11.25: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.
11.26: Then goeth hee, and taketh to him seven other spirites worse then himself: and they enter in, and dwel there: so the last state of that man is worse then the first.
11.27: And it came to pass as he sayde these thinges, a certain woman of the companie lifted up her voyce, and sayde unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the pappes which thou hast sucked.
11.28: But hee said, Yea, rather blessed are they that hear the woorde of God, and keep it.
11.29: And when the people were gathered thick together, he began to say, This is a wicked generation: they seek a sign, and there shall no sign be given them, but the sign of Jonas the Prophet.
11.30: For as Jonas was a sign to the Niniuites: so shall also the Sonne of man bee to this generation.
11.31: The Queen of the South shall rise in iudgement, with the men of this generation, and shall condemn them: for she came from the utmost partes of the earth to hear the wisedome of Salomon, and behold, a greater then Salomon is here.
11.32: The men of Niniue shall rise in iudgement with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas: and behold, a greater then Jonas is here.
11.33: No man when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a priuie place, neither under a bushel: but on a candlestick, that they which come in, may see the light.
11.34: The light of the bodie is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, then is thy whole bodie light: but if thine eye be evil, then thy bodie is dark.
11.35: Take heed therefore, that the light which is in thee, be not darkenesse.
11.36: If therefore thy whole body shall be light, having no part dark, then shall all be light, even as when a candle doth light thee with the brightness.
11.37: And as hee spake, a certain Pharise besought him to dine with him: and hee went in, and sat down at table.
11.38: And when the Pharise saw it, he marueiled that he had not first washed before dinner.
11.39: And the Lord said to him, In deed yee Pharises make clean the outside of the cuppe, and of the platter: but the inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.
11.40: Ye fooles, did not he that made that which is without, make that which is within also?
11.41: Therefore, give almes of those thinges which you have, and behold, all thinges shall be clean to you.
11.42: But wo be to you, Pharises: for ye tithe the mynt and the rewe, and all maner herbs, and pass over iudgement and the love of God: these ought yee to have done, and not to have left the other undone.
11.43: Wo be to you, Pharises: for ye love the uppermost seats in the Synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
11.44: Wo be to you, Scribes and Pharises, hypocrites: for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them, perceive not.
11.45: Then answered one of the Lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou puttest us to rebuke also.
11.46: And he sayde, Wo be to you also, yee Lawyers: for yee lade men with burdens grieuous to be borne, and yee your selves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
11.47: Wo be to you: for ye build the sepulchres of the Prophetes, and your fathers killed them.
11.48: Truely ye bear witness, and allow the deedes of your fathers: for they killed them, and yee build their sepulchres.
11.49: Therefore said the wisedome of God, I wil send them Prophets and Apostles, and of them they shall slaie, and persecute away,
11.50: That the blood of all the Prophets, shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
11.51: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which was slain between the altar and the Temple: verely I say unto you, it shall be required of this generation.
11.52: Wo be to you, Lawyers: for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entred not in your selves, and them that came in, ye forbad.
11.53: And as he sayde these things unto them, the Scribes and Pharises began to urge him sore, and to provoke him to speak of many things,
11.54: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch some thing of his mouth, whereby they might accuse him.

12.1: In the mean time, there gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, so that they trode one another: and he began to say unto his disciples first, Take heed to your selves of the leaven of the Pharises, which is hypocrisie.
12.2: For there is nothing covered, that shall not bee reueiled: neither hid, that shall not be knowen.
12.3: Wherefore whatsoever yee have spoken in darkenesse, it shall be heard in the light: and that which ye have spoken in the ear, in secret places, shall be preached on the houses.
12.4: And I say unto you, my friendes, be not afraid of them that kill the bodie, and after that are not able to doe any more.
12.5: But I wil forewarn you, who ye shall fear: fear him which after hee hath killed, hath power to cast into hell: yea, I say unto you, him fear.
12.6: Are not five sparowes bought for two farthings, and yet not one of them is forgotten before God?
12.7: Yea, and all the heares of your head are nombred: fear not therefore: yee are more of value then many sparowes.
12.8: Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess mee before men, him shall the Sonne of man confess also before the Angels of God.
12.9: But hee that shall denie mee before men, shall be denied before the Angels of God.
12.10: And whosoever shall speak a woorde against the Sonne of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him, that shall blaspheme ye holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven.
12.11: And when they shall bring you unto the Synagogues, and unto the rulers and Princes, take no thought how, or what thing ye shall answer, or what yee shall speak.
12.12: For the holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour, what yee ought to say.
12.13: And one of the companie said unto him, Master, bidde my brother deuide the inheritance with me.
12.14: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge, or a deuider over you?
12.15: Wherefore he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of couetousnesse: for though a man have abundance, yet his life standeth not in his riches.
12.16: And he put foorth a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought foorth fruites plenteously.
12.17: Therefore he thought with himself, saying, What shall I doe, because I have no roume, where I may lay up my fruites?
12.18: And he said, This wil I do, I wil pul down my barnes, and build greater, and therein will I gather all my fruites, and my goods.
12.19: And I wil say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many yeeres: live at ease, eat, drink and take thy pastime.
12.20: But God said unto him, O fool, this night wil they fetch away thy soul from thee: then whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?
12.21: So is he that gathereth riches to himself, and is not rich in God.
12.22: And he spake unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what yee shall eat: neither for your body, what yee shall put on.
12.23: The life is more then meat: and the body more then the raiment.
12.24: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap: which neither have storehouse nor barn, and yet God feedeth them: how much more are yee better then foules?
12.25: And which of you with taking thought, can add to his stature one cubit?
12.26: If yee then bee not able to doe the least thing, why take yee thought for the remnant?
12.27: Consider the lilies how they grow: they labour not, neither spin they: yet I say unto you, that Salomon himself in all his royaltie was not clothed like one of these.
12.28: If then God so clothe the grass which is to day in the field, and to morowe is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O yee of litle faith?
12.29: Therefore ask not what yee shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither hag you in suspense.
12.30: For all such things the people of the world seek for: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.
12.31: But rather seek ye after the kingdom of God, and all these things shalbe cast upon you.
12.32: Fear not, litle flock: for it is your Fathers pleasure, to give you the kingdom.
12.33: Sell that ye have, and give almes: make you bagges, which wax not old, a treasure that can never fail in heaven, where no theefe cometh, neither moth corrupteth.
12.34: For where your treasure is, there will your hearts be also.
12.35: Let your loynes be gird about and your lights burning,
12.36: And ye your selves like unto men that wait for their master, when he will return from the wedding, that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediatly.
12.37: Blessed are those servants, whom the Lord when he cometh shall find waking: verely I say unto you, he will gird himself about, and make them to sit down at table, and will come forth, and serve them.
12.38: And if he come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and shall find them so, blessed are those servants.
12.39: Now understand this, that if the good man of the house had knowen at what hour the theefe would have come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be digged through.
12.40: Be ye also prepared therefore: for the Sonne of man will come at an hour when ye think not.
12.41: Then Peter said unto him, Master, tellest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?
12.42: And the Lord said, Who is a faithful steward and wise, whom the master shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in season?
12.43: Blessed is that servant, whom his master when he cometh, shall find so doing.
12.44: Of a trueth I say unto you, that he wil make him ruler over all that he hath.
12.45: But if that servant say in his heart, My master doeth deferre his coming, and ginne to smite the servants, and maydens, and to eat, and drink, and to be drunken,
12.46: The master of that servant will come in a day when he thinketh not, and at an hour when he is not ware of, and will cut him off, and give him his portion with the vnbeleeuers.
12.47: And that servant that knew his masters will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shalbe beaten with many stripes.
12.48: But he that knew it not, and yet did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes: for unto whomsoever much is given, of him shalbe much required, and to whom men much commit, the more of him will they ask.
12.49: I am come to put fire on the earth, and what is my desire, if it be already kindled?
12.50: Notwithstanding I must be baptized with a baptism, and how am I grieved, till it be ended?
12.51: Think ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, nay, but rather debate.
12.52: For from hencefoorth there shall be five in one house deuided, three against two, and two against three.
12.53: The father shalbe deuided against ye sonne, and the sonne against the father: the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother: the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
12.54: Then said he to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the West, straightway ye say, A shower cometh: and so it is.
12.55: And when ye see the South wind blow, ye say, that it wilbe hoate: and it cometh to pass.
12.56: Hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the earth, and of the skie: but why discern ye not this time?
12.57: Yea, and why judge ye not of your selves what is right?
